concept.name: Pullback
concept.definition: A temporary counter-move against the prevailing trend — typically shallow and short-lived — after which the prior trend resumes. It is an interpretive label: whether a counter-move is a pullback or the start of a reversal is knowable only in hindsight.
concept.intuition: The trend takes a breather: some traders take profits, price slips a little, then the main move continues.
concept.mechanics: Identified as a counter-trend decline in an uptrend (or rally in a downtrend) that stalls at logical areas such as prior support/resistance, moving averages, or Fibonacci retracement zones (often 38.2%-61.8%), and is followed by resumption of the trend. Volume commonly contracts during the pullback and expands on resumption.
concept.failure_modes: Any pullback can deepen into a correction or full reversal; entering on the assumption of resumption fails precisely when the trend is ending.
concept.misconceptions: That pullbacks are safe entries because 'the trend is intact'; trend integrity is only confirmed after the pullback resolves.
concept.example: In an uptrend from 50 to 58, price dips back to 54 (near the 50% retracement and prior breakout level), forms a bullish candle, and then rallies to new highs.

citations.source: Fenefx — What Is a Price Correction or Pullback?
citations.section: A Simple and Precise Definition of Pullback in Financial Markets
